title: Cap. IV Arg. 3 Sol: if Major universal, false — declared beneplacita do not contain formal decree
pass_a_gloss: But let us permit them to act in their own manner: I say, unless the major proposition be universal, from all particulars nothing will follow. If it be universal in this sense, Any, or every, good pleasure of God concerning human salvation is predestination itself to salvation, then it will be manifestly false. For in any declared good pleasure of God concerning human salvation the formal decree of predestination is not straightway expressed or contained. For God has declared in the word the good pleasure of his will concerning the qualities and operations of men to be led to salvation, concerning the means which they ought to use, finally concerning the whole order of executing predestination: yet in these the decree of election is not contained, because they look equally to all, and are proposed after the manner of a law.
pass_b_english: Let them argue their way: unless the Major is universal, nothing follows from particulars. If universal — Any or every good pleasure of God concerning human salvation is predestination itself to salvation — it is manifestly false. In any declared good pleasure about human salvation the formal decree of predestination is not at once expressed or contained. God has declared in the word his will's good pleasure about the qualities and operations of those to be led to salvation, the means they ought to use, and the whole order of executing predestination — yet those do not contain the election decree, because they look equally to all and are set forth as law.
source_text: Sed permittamus eos suo modo agere: dico, nisi major propositio sit universalis, ex omnibus particularibus nihil sequetur. Si sit universalis hoc sensu, Quodlibet, vel omne, beneplacitum Dei de salute humana est ipsa praedestinatio ad salutem, tum erit manifeste falsa. Nam in quovis Dei beneplacito de salute humana declarato, non ilico exprimitur aut continetur formale decretum praedestinationis. Declaravit enim Deus in verbo beneplacitum voluntatis suae de qualitatibus et operationibus hominum ad salutem perducendorum, de mediis quibus eos uti oporteat, denique de toto ordine exsequendae praedestinationis: in hisce tamen non continetur electionis decretum, quia ex aequo ad omnes spectant, et per modum legis proponuntur.
